verbalization: Roxarsone appears to have a complex relationship with Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) through a chain of targets. The evidence suggests that Roxarsone interacts with Gamma-aminobutyric acid type B receptor subunit 1, which in turn is targeted by Protein S human. This protein, in turn, has a target of GAPDH. While the direct interaction between Roxarsone and GAPDH is not explicitly stated, the indirect pathway through Protein S human provides a plausible mechanism for a potential interaction. The scores indicate a moderate confidence in this relationship, suggesting that Roxarsone may influence GAPDH through the intermediate of the GABA-B receptor subunit. This pathway highlights the role of Protein S human as a bridge between Roxarsone and GAPDH, emphasizing the importance of intermediary proteins in drug-target interactions.
